source.note: Confirmed = the domain expert said it in EXPERT.md (2026-07-27). Candidate = only INPUT.md implies it. Expert unavailable for follow-up in this run, so no candidate could be promoted.

timeline.name: whenever a tariff changes, it is live at that site's machines the same evening
whenever a stay is priced: per started 15 min at the site+class rate, with the site's free-first-15, daily cap and night/weekend rates
whenever no bay of the declared class is free, admit to a substitutable class at the declared class's rate; never truck to a car bay
Free bays per level and per type (garage only)
whenever the classes disagree, charge the higher rate at payment and raise a daily exception
BayVacated (garage only; in a lot nothing was held)
whenever the assigned bay is taken anyway, the driver takes the next free one; no consequence, sensors resync
whenever a plate record is 7 days old, delete it (works council, non-negotiable)
no guiding system exists in a lot
LostTicketCharged (flat = daily cap for the class)
whenever more than 15 minutes pass between payment and exit, the exit refuses the card and the difference is paid at a payment machine
never trap a driver: whenever the exit terminal is offline, trust the stripe and open
CardsRefilled (twice a week, from the collected stack)
Reconciliation view (machines vs bank vs coin box)
Occupancy report per bay type over time
whenever occupancy shows a persistent shortage of a type, the operator repaints bays
no machine rule for disabled or family bays; family bays nobody enforces at all
FiscalRecordRetained (site, entry, exit, amount, VAT, method, machine; not the plate)
retention is per country - DE/AT 10y, NL 7y, FR unknown; do not hard-code ten years
Guidance system (cameras, bay sensors, LED signs; 3 suppliers)

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: a uniquely identified place to park; garage = number & floor, lot = number & area
a garage place with a ceiling sensor, individually assignable and releasable
a lot's painted zone; nothing is held, nothing is released
motorcycle, car, electric car, truck/bus, handicapped person, family-friendly
what the vehicle is, and what the tariff is priced by; disabled and family are not in it
a property of the person, not the car - disabled and family bays; unenforceable by machine
the thing collected at the entrance, carrying a spot ID; its information is kept 10 years
the physical reusable plastic with the read/write stripe; ~100 visits over its life
site, entry time, exit time, amount, VAT, payment method, machine paid at; not the plate
the truth
a copy so the machines can be quick; the only authority an offline exit terminal has; rewritable
no bay at all: FULL sign, barrier down, no ticket
no bay of that class: the driver is still admitted to a substitutable bay at their own rate
garage: the sensor says free. Lot: unknowable until somebody walks past
one garage or one lot; the unit of setup, tariffs, reconciliation and occupancy
a site with bay sensors, cameras and guidance signage - a different product from a lot
asphalt and painted lines; no sensors, no guidance, no plate reading
per started 15 minutes, per site and per vehicle class; free-first-15 and daily cap are per-site settings; night/weekend rates at some sites
the most a class can pay in a day at that site; also the flat charge for a lost ticket
the billing increment; 16 minutes bills as two
the 15 minutes allowed between paying and exiting
a button on the payment machine: pay the class's daily cap, get a fresh card that says paid
a barrier opened on the stripe's word alone, logged in the terminal, uploaded when the link returns
the daily list a site manager works: offline exits, plate mismatches, stuck barriers
the usual decision on an unmatched exit
machines vs bank vs coin box, every morning, per site; 4h/week by hand today
how full, per bay type, at a point in time; used against the landlord and to decide repainting
the bought package: cameras, bay sensors, LED signs; one supplier per site
the plate's registered class disagrees with the typed class
the start-up's billing unit, per bay per month
a machine at an entrance, a payment point or an exit; three types named, four behaviours described
what a patrol issues to a car in a disabled bay; the only enforcement that exists
a control-room operator opening a barrier on the intercom when a machine ate the card
